key_insight: Sequential thermal evaporation follows two different solid-state conversion routes in wide-bandgap and narrow-bandgap perovskites, so bandgap control must be tailored to each stack chemistry.
engineering_relevance: This enables solvent-free fabrication of all-perovskite tandems with tunable absorbers, first demonstrating an evaporated tandem at 19.2% efficiency.
method: Time-sliced ex situ analysis of sequentially evaporated precursor stacks
Comparative study of mixed-halide WBG and Sn-Pb NBG solid-state conversion
Guided absorber design across 1.26–1.96 eV bandgaps
evidence_signal: The paper reports a first evaporated all-perovskite tandem solar cell with 19.2% power conversion efficiency and 80% average efficiency retention after 1,200 h at 65 °C.
watch_item: The conversion pathways are highly bandgap- and composition-dependent, so process transfer will likely require tight control of precursor thickness, penetration, and thermal annealing.
paper_title: Divergent Solid-state Conversion Pathways in Evaporated All-perovskite Tandem Solar Cells
